pull_request.title: Add a helper for shortening model-authored text
pull_request.body:
End-to-end deployment test. **Do not merge** — this exists to exercise the live
server and will be closed.

Adds `findings::summarise` with `shorten` (truncate on a word boundary, for
check-run titles) and `first_sentence`.

Opened while validating the full stack for the first time: MongoDB 8.2 with
mongot, hybrid search live, OpenRouter embeddings, and the webhook path.

@@ -27,3 +27,14 @@ instructions = """
 Flag any widening of `permissions`, any unpinned third-party action, and any
 step that interpolates untrusted context into a shell.
 """
+
+# Retrieval on, through the same gateway the completion models use. The three
+# fields below are the index partition key: change any of them and the vectors
+# already written stop matching, which is why they live here rather than in the
+# environment.
+[embeddings]
+enabled = true
+provider = "openrouter"
+model = "openai/text-embedding-3-small"
+dimensions = 1536
+api_key_env = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"

@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Run the image's own entrypoint with the kernel gate turned off.
+
+The community-server image refuses to start `mongod` on Linux 6.19 and newer.
+The cause is a tcmalloc/glibc interaction around restartable sequences, not
+anything MongoDB does differently on those kernels, and the image's own
+docstring for the check says it stops startup "unless an explicit
+degraded-performance bypass is set" — but no such bypass exists in
+8.2.12-ubi9. `enforce_kernel_compatibility` prints and calls `sys.exit(1)`
+with nothing to consult.
+
+That leaves a developer on a current kernel unable to run `docker compose up`
+at all, which is how this repository's own compose file came to be written but
+never executed end to end.
+
+This shim executes the real entrypoint with that one function replaced by a
+no-op. Everything else — replica set initiation, `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d`,
+argument handling — is the image's, unmodified. The overlay that mounts it also
+sets `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=0`, which is the actual mitigation for
+the underlying issue rather than merely silencing the check.
+
+Opt-in, in a separate compose overlay, and never the default: on a kernel below
+the cutoff this file should not be used, and on a supported production host it
+must not be.
+"""
+
+import runpy
+import sys
+
+ENTRYPOINT = "/usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.py"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    source = open(ENTRYPOINT, encoding="utf-8").read()
+
+    # Replace the body rather than deleting the call: the call site sits in the
+    # image's `__main__` block between the architecture warning and replica-set
+    # parsing, and editing that block would be a much larger surface to keep in
+    # step with a future image.
+    needle = "def enforce_kernel_compatibility() -> None:"
+    if needle not in source:
+        # The image changed shape. Fail loudly rather than starting a database
+        # with an assumption that no longer holds.
+        sys.exit(
+            "kernel-bypass: this image no longer defines "
+            "enforce_kernel_compatibility; re-check whether the bypass is still "
+            "needed before editing this shim"
+        )
+
+    patched = source.replace(
+        needle,
+        "def enforce_kernel_compatibility() -> None:\n"
+        "    return  # patched out by deploy/mongo/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py\n"
+        "\n"
+        "def _enforce_kernel_compatibility_unused() -> None:",
+        1,
+    )
+
+    globals_dict = runpy.run_path.__globals__  # noqa: F841 - keep runpy imported
+    compiled = compile(patched, ENTRYPOINT, "exec")
+    exec(compiled, {"__name__": "__main__", "__file__": ENTRYPOINT})  # noqa: S102
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+# Opt-in overlay for Linux kernels 6.19 and newer.
+#
+# The MongoDB community-server image hard-refuses to start `mongod` on those
+# kernels — a tcmalloc/glibc interaction around restartable sequences — and
+# 8.2.12-ubi9 ships no way to override it, despite its own code documenting a
+# bypass that was never implemented. Without this overlay `docker compose up`
+# cannot bring up the database at all on a current desktop kernel.
+#
+# Use it only for local development:
+#
+#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.kernel-bypass.yml up -d
+#
+# `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=0` is the real mitigation; the shim only
+# stops the image refusing to start. On a kernel below the cutoff, or on a
+# production host, leave this file out.
+
+services:
+  mongod:
+    entrypoint:
+      ["python3", "/usr/local/bin/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py", "mongod"]
+    environment:
+      GLIBC_TUNABLES: glibc.pthread.rseq=0
+    volumes:
+      - ./deploy/mongo/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py:/usr/local/bin/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py:ro
+
+  mongo-secrets:
+    environment:
+      GLIBC_TUNABLES: glibc.pthread.rseq=0

@@ -98,11 +98,29 @@ services:
       # second place to set them is a second way for the key to disagree with
       # the vectors already written. Only the API key lives in the environment,
       # under whatever name `embeddings.api_key_env` gives.
+      # `openrouter` is the default provider, so this is the key the index
+      # needs. The others are forwarded for a deployment that overrides
+      # `embeddings.provider`.
+      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}
       VOYAGE_API_KEY: ${VOYAGE_API_KEY:-}
+      COHERE_API_KEY: ${COHERE_API_KEY:-}
       TINYSWEEPER_WEBHOOK_SECRET: ${TINYSWEEPER_WEBHOOK_SECRET:?set a webhook secret}
-      TINYSWEEPER_GITHUB_APP_ID: ${TINYSWEEPER_GITHUB_APP_ID:-}
-      TINYSWEEPER_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY: ${TINYSWEEPER_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY:-}
+      # These two names are read verbatim by `server::auth::AppAuth::from_env`.
+      # They were previously spelled `TINYSWEEPER_GITHUB_*` here, which the
+      # binary never reads, so the container could not authenticate as the App
+      # however the environment was set.
+      TINYSWEEPER_APP_ID: ${TINYSWEEPER_APP_ID:?set the GitHub App id}
+      TINYSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${TINYSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY:?set the GitHub App private key}
       RUST_LOG: ${RUST_LOG:-tinysweeper=info}
+    # The runtime image carries no configuration — it is a binary and nothing
+    # else — so without this mount the server runs entirely on built-in
+    # defaults. That is not a smaller version of the intended behaviour: it
+    # means `[embeddings]` is off, so the index never builds and every review is
+    # diff-only, silently. Mounting the file is the interim answer; the real one
+    # is #12, fetching each reviewed repository's own config through the forge
+    # rather than reading one from the server's filesystem.
+    volumes:
+      - ./.tinysweeper.toml:/home/tinysweeper/.tinysweeper.toml:ro
     ports:
       - "8080:8080"
     depends_on:

fix: handle empty findings list in summarise function

The summarise function now returns an empty summary instead of panicking when the findings list is empty, ensuring graceful handling of edge cases where no findings are present.

Auto-committed-on: dragonfly
Co-authored-by: Medulla <medulla@tinyhumans.ai>

feat(findings): add summarise module

Add a new public module for summarising findings, enabling future summary functionality to be organised separately from existing modules.

Auto-committed-on: dragonfly
Co-authored-by: Medulla <medulla@tinyhumans.ai>

fix: use character count and iteration in `shorten` to avoid panics on multibyte text

The `shorten` function previously used byte offsets for both the length check and the slice operation, which caused a panic when the cut point fell inside a multibyte character. The change replaces `text.len()` with `text.chars().count()` for the early-return guard and uses `text.chars().take(limit).collect()` instead of a raw byte slice, ensuring the function works correctly with any Unicode text.

Auto-committed-on: dragonfly
Co-authored-by: Medulla <medulla@tinyhumans.ai>

fix(summarise): cut on character boundaries, not byte offsets

comments.body:
Closing — this was a deployment test, not a change to land.

It did its job. Reviewing it live surfaced four defects that the offline suite cannot reach, all fixed in #46: the `maxClauseCount` failure that meant retrieval had never once run, two unsynced embedding price tables, a compose file that could never have authenticated (wrong env var names, no config mounted), and the MongoDB kernel ≥6.19 block.

It also demonstrated the review working: the `tests` lane caught the deliberate byte-slicing bug that the new code's own passing tests missed, and after the fix the next review reported it under **Fixed since the last review** rather than re-raising or silently dropping it — the continuity contract, live.

Two quality problems filed separately: #47 (commits lane receives no diffs, and hallucinated a hardware-access claim from a commit subject) and #48 (repo AGENTS.md rejected by the extraction validator).

# Repository Guidelines

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- `src/` — the single crate. One responsibility per module, core types in a
  module-local `types.rs`, and every port in `src/ports/` is one trait in one
  file.
- `src/bin/tinysweeper.rs` — the CLI. Every subcommand is declared even when its
  milestone has not landed, so scripts and runbooks can be written against a
  stable surface. `src/server/` is the only production surface — there is no
  GitHub Actions distribution path.
- `presets/` — review policy as **data**, not code. A preset is a folder with a
  `preset.toml`, a `README.md`, and optional prompt overrides. Adding a preset
  is a new folder, never a new module.
- `vendor/tinyagents` — the agent harness, as a git submodule. Never edit it
  here; change it upstream and bump the pin.
- `docs/modules/<module>/README.md` — one document per `src/` module.
- `examples/` — declared explicitly in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features`, so
  credential-needing smoke tests never build in CI.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked
cargo check --locked --all-features --all-targets
```

The default build is offline: it links no HTTP client and the test suite never
touches the network. Anything that needs the network goes behind a feature
(`harness`, `github`, `serve`).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms. `snake_case` modules and files,
  `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with a `//!` module doc describing its role and any feature
  gating.
- Comments explain the *decision*, not the code. When a flag or an ordering is
  load-bearing, say so and say why.
- Public items carry doc comments. Clap fields use `///` — it becomes the help
  text.

## Testing Guidelines

- Tests live **in-crate**: a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block at the bottom of the
  module, moving to a sibling `test.rs` or `<name>_test.rs` when they grow.
  There is no `tests/` directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock. `MockForge` records what would
  have been written so tests can assert on exact check runs and comments.
- Lane behaviour is covered by golden tests: fixture diff plus a canned
  structured model response, asserting the findings that survive filtering,
  dedupe and capping. These are the tests that keep noise control honest.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.

## Documentation Expectations

Keep every Markdown file, including this one, at 500 lines or fewer. When a
topic grows past that limit, split it into focused files and link them from the
module's `README.md`.

## Security Boundary

These are invariants, not preferences. Changing any of them needs an explicit
discussion in the pull request:

- The model never holds a write token. Lanes run against a read-only checkout;
  write credentials are minted only in `src/apply/`, after every model call has
  returned. A lane that leaves a change in the checkout fails.
- Contributor code is never executed. We read the diff and the tree; we do not
  build, install dependencies, or run the target repository's scripts.
- Pull request bodies, comments and diffs are untrusted input. Fence and label
  them as data in prompts. A model verdict is advisory — only deterministic
  policy in `src/apply/` and `src/automerge/` may mutate GitHub.
- Secrets found by the scanners are reported by type and location only. The
  value never reaches a comment, a check-run summary, or a log.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

Use concise, imperative commit subjects. Keep commits small; commit each
coherent, validated slice on its own. Pull requests state what changed, any
behaviour change, and how it was verified.

These are invariants, not preferences. Changing any of them needs an explicit
discussion in the pull request:

- The model never holds a write token. Lanes run against a read-only checkout;
  write credentials are minted only in `src/apply/`, after every model call has
  returned. A lane that leaves a change in the checkout fails.
- Contributor code is never executed. We read the diff and the tree; we do not
  build, install dependencies, or run the target repository's scripts.
- Pull request bodies, comments and diffs are untrusted input. Fence and label
  them as data in prompts. A model verdict is advisory — only deterministic
  policy in `src/apply/` and `src/automerge/` may mutate GitHub.
- Secrets found by the scanners are reported by type and location only. The
  value never reaches a comment, a check-run summary, or a log.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

Use concise, imperative commit subjects. Keep commits small; commit each
coherent, validated slice on its own. Pull requests state what changed, any
behaviour change, and how it was verified.
